The latch campaign prices usable demonstrations in scheduled time and component wear, distinguishes expert intent from permission-path correction, and joins the archive against required fixture conditions. In the illustrative budget, less than a quarter of scheduled time survives as retained demonstration motion; that cost makes targeted recovery collection more informative than repeating only the nominal approach. Records also stay bound to the body and calibration that produced them. Normalizing another machine's labels does not make them executable, and a shifted camera or a worn pad changes what an unchanged file means. The provenance record preserves what each archive contains and omits. The stipulated recovery extension shows how to add correctly attributed experience without rewriting the original record. Recovery data has value only where an expert can still undo a mistake: the recoverability constant of the aggregation bound grows without limit at irreversible states, which therefore belong to the permission path rather than to the dataset. Whether a candidate learns the recovery, preserves nominal performance, and merits a wider operating claim remains a training and evaluation decision.

The equations behind these decisions are gathered in @tbl-05-key-equations, each with what it bounds or decides and where it is derived.

| Equation                                                                                                                                                              | What it bounds or decides                                                                                                                  | Derived in                     |
|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| $J(\pi)-J(\pi^*) \le T^2\epsilon$                                                                                                                                     | The worst-case excess cost of cloning on expert states under a 0–1 action loss; it says nothing once $\epsilon > 1/T$                      | @eq-data-quadratic-drift       |
| $J(\hat{\pi}) \le J(\pi^*) + u\,T\,\epsilon_N + O(1)$                                                                                                                 | The cost after aggregating expert labels on learner-visited states, linear in $T$ only while the recoverability constant $u$ stays bounded | @eq-data-dagger-bound          |
| $N_{\text{eff}} = N(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)$                                                                                                                                 | How many independent observations a serially correlated telemetry stream holds for one statistic                                           | @eq-data-effective-sample-size |
| $\Delta\mathbf{x}_{\text{sync}} \approx \mathbf{v}\,\Delta t_{\text{lag}}$                                                                                            | The position error a pairing lag injects, and so the largest lag a task clearance tolerates                                                | @eq-data-sync-displacement     |
| $\Delta t_{\text{skew}} = (H-1)\,\tau_{\text{line}}$                                                                                                                  | The time spread across one rolling-shutter frame, which a moving arm turns into shape distortion                                           | @eq-data-rolling-shutter-skew  |
| $t_{\text{loop}} = t_{\text{disp}} + t_{\text{hum}} + t_{\text{cmd}} + t_{\text{mech}}$                                                                               | The phase lag a teleoperated demonstration carries between a state and the correction chosen for it                                        | @eq-data-teleop-loop-latency   |
| $Y_{\text{usable}} = \lfloor T_{\text{motion}}/t_{\text{cyc}} \rfloor R$                                                                                              | Retained demonstrations per scheduled session, and so the cell time and wear a campaign target costs                                       | @eq-data-demonstration-yield   |
| $\hat{t}_{\text{div}}$: first threshold crossing in $[t_{\text{takeover}} - \Delta t_{\text{lookback}},\, t_{\text{takeover}}]$                                       | Where the masked drift window begins, and whether the lookback reaches back far enough to find it                                          | @eq-data-divergence-point      |
| $\epsilon_{\text{reproj}} = \lVert \mathbf{u}_{\text{observed}} - \pi_{\mathbf{K}}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{cam} \leftarrow \text{base}}\,\mathbf{FK}(\mathbf{q})) \rVert_2$ | Whether a session's camera calibration still agrees with the joint encoders                                                                | @eq-data-reprojection-residual |

: **Key equations of physical data**: Each load-bearing equation of the chapter, the limit it bounds or the decision it settles, and the equation where it is derived. {#tbl-05-key-equations tbl-colwidths="[40,42,18]"}

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Physical data collection and provenance"}
* **Coverage counts configurations, not samples:** Repeated nominal motions add rows without adding scenario cells, and adjacent control steps are near duplicates. A dataset's reach is its join against a scenario ledger spanning the ODD, never its sample count or the extremes it happened to log.
* **Validation loss cannot see a coverage gap:** A held-out split shares the collector's occupancy, so near-zero validation loss can coexist with most required cells empty. Only the join against an external ledger exposes the gap.
* **Every action tap is a different signal:** The request, the mapped setpoint, the enforced command, and the measured response differ wherever the permission path or the body intervenes. Keeping the other taps and their timing makes the chosen supervisory target interpretable and preserves evidence of intervention.
* **Keep failures and takeovers, correctly attributed:** Censoring aborted runs erases the states nearest the boundary. Learner commands before a takeover stay in the record for audit and expert relabeling but never as expert labels, and only the stabilized, reviewed part of the recovery after it becomes a separate expert sequence.
* **Data stays bound to the body that collected it:** Camera geometry can be reprojected, but contact wear, compliance, and backlash are baked into force and tactile labels. Data from a changed or different body requires revalidation, and range normalization hides the mismatch rather than removing it.
* **New experience can expand the claim:** An immutable record describes one archive, not a permanent limit on learning. New recovery data receives new provenance; a wider competence claim requires a trained candidate and closed-loop evidence under the added conditions.
:::

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-data-history}

Demonstration began as remote manipulation. Goertz's master-slave manipulators at Argonne moved tongs behind radiation shielding in exact correspondence with a handle, and the mechanical linkage returned the contact forces to the operator's hand [@goertz1949master]. Once electronics and distance separated the two arms, that force channel became a control problem. @anderson1989bilateral showed that a delayed link can destabilize a bilateral teleoperator and restored passivity for any constant delay, and @niemeyer1991stable recast the remedy as wave variables; @hokayem2006bilateral trace the line from Goertz to these delay-robust schemes. Every collection interface in this chapter sits somewhere on the trade those papers exposed, between a stable loop and faithful contact force, and the demonstrations it records carry that choice.

Learning a controller from those recordings has an equally direct lineage. ALVINN learned to steer a van from a human driver's camera images and met the recovery gap at once, because the driver never let the van drift [@pomerleau1989alvinn; @pomerleau1991efficient]. Robot learning from demonstration grew into a field of its own, organized by how demonstrations are gathered and how a policy is derived from them [@argall2009survey]. @ross2010efficient gave the quadratic bound for cloning on the expert's states, and @ross2011reduction gave the linear bound for aggregating expert labels on the learner's states, conditional on a recoverability constant. Human-gated aggregation and noise injection during collection adapted that result to experts who are people rather than oracles [@kelly2019hgdagger; @laskey2017dart], and the curation rules of @sec-data-intervention-recovery descend from them.

The accounting of coverage borrows from older fields. @bellman1957dynamic named the curse of dimensionality for tables indexed by state, climatologists corrected the sample sizes of serially correlated records [@thiebaux1984interpretation], and Wald's wartime analysis of returning aircraft showed what a sample filtered by survival cannot contain [@mangel1984wald]. Robot learning met all three as datasets grew from single laboratories to pooled corpora collected across many robots and scenes [@walke2023bridgedata; @khazatsky2024droid; @open_x_embodiment_collaboration2024open]. Pooling bought conditions that no single rig could supply. It did not supply a compatibility contract or a record of what each archive leaves out, and dataset documentation [@gebru2021datasheets] was the first attempt at the second. The provenance record of @sec-data-schema extends that documentation to the plant, the action taps, and the known absences.

The readings below run from remote manipulation to pooled robot corpora.

- @hokayem2006bilateral surveys bilateral teleoperation from the first mechanical manipulators through passivity-based designs for delay, and explains why force fidelity and stability trade against each other at the collection interface.
- @pomerleau1991efficient shows, in a few pages, the recovery gap in its first practical form, together with the synthetic remedy that worked because the missing states were only viewpoints.
- @argall2009survey organizes robot learning from demonstration by how data is gathered and how a policy is derived, including the mapping between the demonstrator's body and the robot's that @sec-data-cross-embodiment treats as a contract.
- @ross2011reduction introduces DAgger and states the recoverability constant on which the linear bound depends. It is the source of @eq-data-dagger-bound.
- @open_x_embodiment_collaboration2024open describes a pooled corpus from many robots, and is worth reading for what its authors chose not to align as much as for its results.
- @gebru2021datasheets lists the questions a dataset's documentation should answer. Read against @tbl-05-provenance-schema, it shows which questions a physical archive adds.

## Problems {#sec-data-problems}

```{python}
#| label: calc-data-problems
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ GIVENS FOR THE END-OF-CHAPTER PROBLEMS (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-data-problems.
# │ Goal:    Hold the givens the problems add to the chapter's cells: the
# │          compute module's memory, the navigation camera's readout time,
# │          an illustrative wrist-camera geometry for reprojection, an
# │          illustrative takeover trace, a chosen per-cell requirement, and
# │          the transfer source (a bimanual leader-follower arm cell).
# │          Answers are not printed; the private solution script computes them.
# │ Show:    64 GiB; 16.6 ms; 900 px, 0.60 m, 3 mm, 0.5 deg, 1.5 px; drift
# │          window = design out-of-loop takeover; 1.5 s and 6.0 s after takeover;
# │          2 s short lookback; N_min = 50; ALOHA 14 DoF at 50 Hz, 0.5 kg.
# │ How:     Registry reads (RM, AISLE, Embodied.Manipulator); other givens are
# │          labeled illustrative or chosen in the problem text.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_int, fmt_memory_capacity, fmt_latency, fmt_length, fmt_frequency, fmt_mass, fmt_time, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class DataProblems:
    """Givens that the chapter's problems add beyond the worked examples."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    soc_mem = RM.brain_soc.memory.capacity  # category: datasheet
    nav_readout = RM.nav_camera.readout_time  # category: datasheet
    f_px = 900.0  # wrist-camera focal length in pixels; category: illustrative
    z_work = 0.60 * meter  # camera-to-gripper working distance; category: illustrative
    shift = 3.0 * millimeter  # bracket shift, as in @sec-data-plant-drift; category: illustrative
    tilt_deg = 0.5  # bracket tilt in degrees, as in @sec-data-plant-drift; category: illustrative
    thresh_px = 1.5  # session reprojection threshold; category: illustrative
    t_drift = AISLE.t_takeover_out_of_loop  # category: derived (sourced p90 take-over time + transport)
    t_stab = 1.5 * second  # stabilization after takeover; category: illustrative
    t_rec = 6.0 * second  # latch release after takeover; category: illustrative
    lookback_short = 2.0 * second  # category: illustrative
    servo = RM.permission_rate  # category: datasheet
    n_min = 50  # retained demonstrations per ledger cell; category: chosen
    src = Embodied.Manipulator.ALOHA_Bimanual  # category: literature
    arm = RM.arm  # category: datasheet

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    lookback = AISLE.pre_trigger_window
    reproj_shift = f_px * (shift / z_work).to("").magnitude  # checked, not printed

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(
        RM.nav_camera.shutter_type == "rolling" and RM.wrist_camera.shutter_type == "global",
        "Problem 3 assumes a rolling navigation camera and a global-shutter wrist camera",
    )
    check(t_drift < lookback, "Problem 7: the drift window must fit the design lookback")
    check(t_drift > lookback_short, "Problem 7: the short lookback must lose the divergence point")
    check(t_rec > t_stab, "Recovery must end after stabilization")
    check(reproj_shift > thresh_px, "Problem 6: the 3 mm shift must exceed the threshold")
    check(n_min > DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_usable, "Problem 8: one cell should need more than one session")
    check(src.control_frequency < servo and src.dofs != arm.dofs, "Problem 9 needs a slower, topologically different source")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    soc_mem_str = fmt_memory_capacity(soc_mem, unit=GiB, precision=0)
    nav_readout_str = fmt_latency(nav_readout, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    f_px_str = fmt_int(int(f_px))
    z_work_str = fmt_length(z_work, unit=meter, precision=2)
    shift_str = fmt_length(shift, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    tilt_str = fmt(tilt_deg, precision=1)
    thresh_str = fmt(thresh_px, precision=1)
    t_drift_str = fmt_time(t_drift, unit=second, precision=3)
    t_stab_str = fmt_time(t_stab, unit=second, precision=1)
    t_rec_str = fmt_time(t_rec, unit=second, precision=0)
    lookback_short_str = fmt_time(lookback_short, unit=second, precision=0)
    servo_str = fmt_frequency(servo, unit=ureg.kilohertz, precision=0)
    n_min_str = fmt_int(n_min)
    src_dofs_str = fmt_int(src.dofs)
    src_rate_str = fmt_frequency(src.control_frequency, precision=0)
    src_payload_str = fmt_mass(src.payload_capacity, unit=kilogram, precision=1)
    arm_dofs_str = fmt_int(arm.dofs)
    arm_payload_str = fmt_mass(arm.payload_capacity, unit=kilogram, precision=0)
```

These problems use the running machine's parameters from this chapter's worked examples, with values marked illustrative standing in for measurements as they do there. Each problem names the decision it requires. The tags give the kind of work, from computation through design to critique, and the learning objectives, counted in order, that it assesses.

1. **[Compute, LO3] The reset tax.** For the session of \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}, a quicker re-latch fixture would halve the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_rst_str` reset, while a better strike-plate guide would instead halve the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.failure_pct_str` percent in-trial failure rate. For each change alone, use @eq-data-demonstration-yield to recompute the attempts per session, the scheduled cell time for `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` retained demonstrations, and the percent of the flex cable's rated life the campaign consumes. Decide which change to fund when cell time binds, and which when the cable binds.
2. **[Compute, LO5] Sizing the pre-trigger buffer.** The logger of @sec-data-intervention-recovery must hold a `{python} DataLookbackWindow.t_lookback_str` lookback. Size that buffer for the kinematic stream alone (`{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bytes_per_step_str` bytes per step at `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.f_log_str`), for every stream at the raw `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bw_total_str` of \ref{nbk-data-ingestion-bandwidth-storage-budgets-multi-camera}, and for the session compressed to `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bw_compressed_str`. Compare each with the `{python} DataProblems.soc_mem_str` memory of the machine's compute module, and decide which streams belong in the locked, pre-allocated ring buffer.
3. **[Compute, LO2] Rolling shutter at the latch.** The navigation camera reads out its rows over `{python} DataProblems.nav_readout_str` (datasheet), while the wrist camera exposes every row at once. Treating that readout as the full-frame skew of @eq-data-rolling-shutter-skew, find the displacement across one navigation frame at `{python} SyncDisplacement.v_transit_str` and at both latch approaches, compare each with the `{python} SyncDisplacement.clearance_str` clearance, and find the fastest approach at which navigation frames can serve as latch observations without a row-time correction.
4. **[Compute, LO1] Effective samples in the latch archive.** Apply @eq-data-effective-sample-size with $\rho =$ `{python} EffectiveSampleSize.rho_str` to the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` retained demonstrations of `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str` each, logged at `{python} EffectiveSampleSize.f_log_str`. Compare the campaign's record count, its effective sample size, its episode count, and the share of the latch scenario ledger it occupies (@fig-05-collector-coverage-ledger). State which of these quantities limits what a policy trained on the archive can do at a displaced strike plate, and why none of the others can reveal that limit.
5. **[Compute, LO1] When the bound says nothing.** A latch attempt lasts `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str`. At the illustrative `{python} BoundComparison.f_ctrl_str` control rate of the comparison after @eq-data-dagger-bound, find the horizon $T$, the per-step error above which @eq-data-quadratic-drift is vacuous, and both bounds at $\epsilon =$ `{python} BoundComparison.eps_str` with $u = 1$. Explain why $\epsilon_N$ is not the same quantity as $\epsilon$, and what happens to the comparison if $u$ grows in proportion to $T$.
6. **[Compute, LO7] A bumped bracket in pixels.** A wrist camera with an illustrative focal length of `{python} DataProblems.f_px_str` px views the gripper at an illustrative working distance of `{python} DataProblems.z_work_str`. With the pinhole model of @sec-data-plant-drift, estimate the reprojection residual (@eq-data-reprojection-residual) that a `{python} DataProblems.shift_str` lateral bracket shift produces, and separately a `{python} DataProblems.tilt_str`° tilt. The session check flags residuals above an illustrative `{python} DataProblems.thresh_str` px. Find the smallest lateral shift the check detects, and decide whether it catches a calibration error as large as the latch's `{python} SyncDisplacement.clearance_str` clearance.
7. **[Design, LO5] Curating one takeover.** In an illustrative `latch-recovery-02` episode, the gripper's lateral error first crosses the chosen threshold $\delta_{\text{tol}}$ one design out-of-loop takeover time, `{python} DataProblems.t_drift_str`, before the operator's override at $t_{\text{takeover}}$. The operator's measured stabilization comes `{python} DataProblems.t_stab_str` after takeover, and the latch releases `{python} DataProblems.t_rec_str` after it. The logger ticks at `{python} DataProblems.servo_str`, and the learner issued commands at `{python} BoundComparison.f_ctrl_str`. Lay out the intervals of @fig-05-compounding-error-flywheel on this timeline, count the logged states eligible for expert relabeling and the learner commands to mask, give the length of the admitted expert segment, and check the drift window against the `{python} DataLookbackWindow.t_lookback_str` lookback. Then state what a `{python} DataProblems.lookback_short_str` lookback would lose and how the curation must treat such an episode.
8. **[Design, LO4] A pad-wear axis.** Add a pad-wear axis (new and worn) to the latch ledger of @fig-05-collector-coverage-ledger, and take $N_{\min} =$ `{python} DataProblems.n_min_str` retained demonstrations per cell as a chosen requirement. Assuming the original campaign used new pads throughout, list the supported cells and known absences of the original archive and of its `latch-recovery-02` successor. Using the retained yield per session of \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}, find how many sessions fill one empty cell to $N_{\min}$, and propose the next session, stating which cells remain permission-path territory rather than collection targets.
9. **[Design, LO6] Borrowing from a bimanual arm cell.** A team proposes adding door-opening demonstrations recorded on a bimanual leader-follower arm cell (`{python} DataProblems.src_dofs_str` degrees of freedom across two arms and their grippers, commands at `{python} DataProblems.src_rate_str`, payload `{python} DataProblems.src_payload_str`) to the running machine's latch data. The target arm has `{python} DataProblems.arm_dofs_str` joints, a `{python} DataProblems.arm_payload_str` payload, and a `{python} DataProblems.servo_str` permission tick. Decide which gate of @sec-data-kinematic-topology the records must pass for pretraining and for use as target labels. For target labels, name the action representation that can carry them across, what the target's inverse kinematics must supply that the source never recorded, and the hold lag implied by each side's command period (half the period, @sec-appendix-control-zoh); then classify the approach, contact, and latch-release segments as admitted, relabeled, or rejected.
10. **[Design, LO8] The successor's provenance record.** Write the provenance record for `latch-recovery-02`, filling every field group of @tbl-05-provenance-schema with the chapter's values or an explicit "to be measured". Show how its supported cells and known absences differ from the original record's, what its collection-mode and intervention fields must hold under the curation rules of @sec-data-intervention-recovery, and how it refers to the original archive without rewriting it.
11. **[Critique, LO1, LO4] A large archive with a small loss.** A team presents the cautious collector's archive of @tbl-data-collector-coverage-ledger, with its low held-out loss, as ready for autonomous contact work. Critique the claim: identify what the loss was measured on, what share of the required grid the archive occupies, and which absence mechanisms of @sec-data-intervention-recovery could explain the empty cells. Write three questions the team must answer before any deployment claim, with the evidence each requires.
12. **[Critique, LO3, LO7] A plan budgeted in demonstration time.** A proposal budgets `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` latch demonstrations as `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` $\times$ `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str` of operator time and schedules one camera calibration at the start of the campaign. Critique the budget against \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}: compute the planned demonstration time, the scheduled cell time the illustrative session implies, and their ratio, and name the wear the plan omits. Then state which drift a single calibration cannot detect over the campaign's `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_sched_campaign_str` of cell time, and what checks the plan must add (@sec-data-plant-drift).

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From demonstrations to policies"}
Which source of experience can teach a policy the recoveries its demonstrations never showed? The original latch campaign's provenance record contains demonstrations only for the nominal strike plate at the guarded approach and lists every other cell as a known absence. @Sec-training compares the learning regimes that can address the gap and carries the stipulated `latch-recovery-02` archive into a new candidate. Its policy manifest separates the requested evaluation domain from the capability already supported by evidence; @sec-evaluation tests whether the added experience earns a broader claim.
:::
